New restricted four-state law requires both of two binary vertex bits to change at nonzero-target arrows, giving a single-commutator condition \(\chi(H_z)\le2\) and width \(\lceil\log_2\chi(H_z)\rceil\).

originality.rationale: A complete formula for all constrained prescribed fibers and field-independent binary chromatic width is not a restatement of the older arbitrary-element quiver commutator/Tutte law (whose color threshold is \(q^2\)): their conditions differ on a triangle. Existing single-idempotent cut counts, ring-wide invertibility characterizations, and singular-equivalence results do not provide this constrained distribution. The 2002 general characterization was abstract-only and may cover portions of the existence test; comprehensive priority is not assured.

value.rationale: Restriction of both inputs to idempotents is a natural ring-theoretic factorization problem. The result determines every target multiplicity for all finite loopless quivers and shows that the exact minimal restricted commutator length is \(\lceil\log_2\chi\rceil\), independent of field size, yielding an arbitrarily large separation from unrestricted width over any fixed finite field. These are structural all-family consequences, not small parameter gains.
